phase: DRP4 / B5 — the ingestion recipes actually execute
verdict: CLEARED for the two recipes that can run outside the VPC; the other two are blocked by design, not by a defect
before: the recipes had never been executed. The catalogue was populated by the governance publisher, so nothing had ever proved the recipes were runnable.

environment.why_a_venv: the system install had an incompatible sqlglot and EVERY ingestion source failed to import with `module 'sqlglot.expressions' has no attribute 'Expr'`. A pinned venv fixes it without disturbing the user's packages.

glue.source: real AWS Glue, 83 tables across 6 databases
glue.note: first run used a file sink to prove execution without DataHub (491 events); then the live REST sink

kafka.reason: MSK brokers resolve to PRIVATE addresses (10.42.12.173, 10.42.11.19) on port 9098 and are unreachable from the workstation — verified by TCP connect, not assumed.
kafka.verdict: this is security invariant 3 working as intended (private brokers, no public access). Running it needs an in-VPC host.

kafka-connect.reason: the Connect REST endpoint is private for the same reason

defects_found_by_running.defect: the dbt recipe cannot run to a file sink at all
defects_found_by_running.detail: write_semantics: PATCH calls ctx.require_graph(), so the recipe REQUIRES a live DataHub. `ConfigurationError: Using dbt with write_semantics=PATCH requires a graph`. The PATCH choice is correct (ADR-088 — ingestion must not clobber derived ownership); what was not recorded is that it makes the recipe undeployable without a running GMS.

defects_found_by_running.defect: convert_urns_to_lowercase was being DEFAULTED on the dbt recipe
defects_found_by_running.detail: the CLI warns it 'defaults to true for this source but is not set in the recipe'. A default is exactly what ADR-090 refuses: if dbt lowercases a urn and Glue does not, one table becomes two urns and the graph splits at the CURATED -> MART hop into halves that each look complete.
defects_found_by_running.action: pinned False explicitly on the dbt recipe

defects_found_by_running.detail: setting it there failed with `Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden]`. That is how we learned the Glue side has no such switch and never lowercases — so False on dbt MATCHES Glue rather than being a preference. Found by running the recipe, not by reading documentation.

open.dbt_catalog_incomplete: dbt/target/catalog.json is 269 bytes; `dbt docs generate` has not been run, so schema metadata for several mart models is missing. The ingestion warns 'Node missing from catalog'. Not a blocker for lineage, which comes from the manifest.
